key_insight: Active learning makes interatomic-potential training more data-efficient by selecting new reference calculations for the conditions where a model will be used.
engineering_relevance: Uncertainty-driven sampling can focus expensive reference calculations on configurations relevant to mechanics, diffusion, functional materials, and reactive dynamics.
method: Generate candidate atomic configurations and select informative samples.
Run reference calculations, update the potential, and repeat.
Use committee, Gaussian-process, pretrained-representation, or reaction-aware acquisition strategies.
evidence_signal: The review surveys more than 70 studies, emphasizing 2020–2026, but the abstract reports no pooled quantitative efficiency or accuracy benchmark.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are architecture-dependent and may be least reliable in unfamiliar regimes where dependable selection matters most.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
